new_statements.quote: A word is bordered by word juncture (which is characterized by potential pause) and marked by primary stress on the ultima. Word juncture is represented by space. Primary stress is characterized by volume, usually on the lowest pitch level of the speaker, but varying with the type of intonation contour. It is perhaps best described as a low push. Secondary stress accompanied by a rise in pitch occurs on long vowels. Because of its length and higher pitch characteristics, it sounds, to American ears hearing it for the first time, like primary stress.
new_statements.citation: Whittle, Claudia & Ruth Lusted. 1963. Interaction of coexistent phonemic systems in Atta (Northern Cagayan Negrito). In Elmer Wolfenden (ed.), Papers on Philippine Languages No. 1, 26-39. Manila: Institute for Language Teaching & Summer Institute of Linguistics.

new_statements.rule_in_words: In (Pamplona) Atta every word carries primary stress (a low-pitched intensity 'push') on its final syllable; what sounds like non-final stress is analysed as contrastive vowel length, long vowels bearing a secondary stress with raised pitch (e.g. Spanish vaca > ba:ka). NOTE: this describes the Pamplona dialect (Pamplona Atta, pamp1244), the closest described relative; no statement exists for Faire Atta itself, whose 1981 SIL wordlist marks accents on both penults and finals.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Secondary stress, accompanied by a pitch rise, falls on long vowels (length contrastive for a, i, u; e and o always long); stressed vowels of Spanish loans are borrowed as long vowels with this secondary stress + high pitch (sec. 3.6).
new_statements.exceptions: None for primary stress (stated as always on the ultima); length restricted to the second vowel of a vowel cluster; e/o always long.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain = the word as bounded by potential pause (word juncture); primary stress interacts with intonation contour. Statement is for the Pamplona dialect of Atta (authors list Allacapan, Marag, Pamplona dialects; Faire/Santo Niño Atta is not among them and is a separate Glottolog language fair1238).
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted stress statement (Whittle & Lusted 1963) describes the PAMPLONA dialect of Atta = Pamplona Atta, Glottolog pamp1244 / ISO att (authors: dialects Allacapan, Marag, Pamplona; paper treats Pamplona). Faire Atta (fair1238, azt; Santo Niño/Faire and Rizal, Cagayan) is a separate Glottolog language in the same Atta subgroup and has NO description beyond three SIL wordlists (Nickell 1981 Calassitan; SIL 1960-80 Bullakit; Nickell 1981 Annip, Rizal - the last possibly not Atta at all: SIL record says no ISO code, and the Calassitan sheet says Rizal speech is called 'Imalaweg', i.e. Malaweg/Itawis area). The Faire wordlist accents fall on both penults and finals, which under Whittle & Lusted's analysis would be long-vowel secondary stress vs. final primary stress, but no source says so for Faire Atta. The Whittle & Lusted PDF and PL C-22 were also copied to with a note, since the earlier scan marked that paper SOURCE-NAMED-UNREACHABLE for pamp1244.

sources.locator: sec. 2.1, p. 28 (PDF p. 3; page image); dialect identification p. 26; vowel length p. 30; loanword stress sec. 3.6 pp. 37-38
sources.note: PAMPLONA dialect of Atta (= pamp1244), explicitly (p. 26: three dialects Allacapan, Marag, Pamplona; 'this paper deals with the dialect spoken in Pamplona'). Sec. 2.1 p. 28: word 'marked by primary stress on the ultima' (a 'low push'); secondary stress with pitch rise on long vowels, which to American ears sounds like primary stress; vowel length contrastive on a i u (e, o always long) p. 30; length also a plural morpheme (lala:ki/lalla:ki); sec. 3.6 pp. 37-38: Spanish penult-stressed vowels are borrowed as long vowels with secondary stress + high pitch (vaca > ba:ka).
